rationale: The study reports inferential Pearson correlations, ANOVA, and simple linear regression on a survey of N = 379 households in Matungulu Sub-County, Kenya, but fails SWiM eligibility on both Criterion 4 and narrow Criterion 2. In every inferential test (Tables 2-6, pp. 5, 8-10), the dependent variable is a composite score of general 'Impact on Household Livelihoods' rather than a household or community water/sanitation service access outcome (connection, coverage, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, or affordability). Furthermore, the predictor ('Integration of RHT in County Development Agenda') is a respondent Likert-scale perception score of county programmatic extension/project activities (farmer training, water pan/dam excavation, group funding, awareness creation, and tank provision) rather than an empirical contrast across a rule-type legal, regulatory, tenure, or tariff mechanism, while all household RHT adoption/financing breakdowns (Figures 2-5, Table 1) are purely descriptive percentages and means.
